statements.text: Substance dualism is the view that minds and bodies are fundamentally distinct kinds of substance, as Plato, Augustine and Descartes held. Swinburne defines a substance as a thing, a component of the world such as a table, a star or a person, and defends the view that each human on Earth consists of a physical body and a nonphysical soul.

sources.quote: by ‘substance dualism’ we mean the view that minds and bodies are fundamentally distinct kinds of substances
I seek in this paper to defend the view that each of us on Earth consists of two parts - a physical body and a non-physical soul.
